scope: One public synthetic Python project; not a model-quality benchmark.

primary_finding.classification: Model output exceeded the frozen per-worker response allowance; existing runtime rejected the incomplete tool response without dispatch.

subsequent_sequence.event: Parent proposed a replacement parser child
Parent ran full acceptance and CLI against unchanged parser stub
Parent marked its goal blocked and reported partial delivery
Independent runner evaluated original acceptance files

diagnostic_wording_boundary.original_child_text: Model response incomplete: finish_reason=length; no tools executed.
diagnostic_wording_boundary.literal_scope: No tools executed refers to the one incomplete model response rejected by agent/session.py before canonical assistant/tool-group admission.
diagnostic_wording_boundary.whole_child_scope: The child had already completed four read-only tool calls: read SPEC.md, parser.py, tests/test_acceptance.py, and list fixtures.
diagnostic_wording_boundary.parent_misinterpretation: The final parent answer says the assigned child failed before executing any tools. The four earlier completed receipts contradict that broader statement.

product_and_environment_assessment.output_guard: Rejecting a truncated tool call before dispatch is existing behavior; this run does not establish a new tool execution defect.
product_and_environment_assessment.recovery_limit: The existing runtime stops this child after a length-truncated tool response instead of asking the same child to split its next patch within remaining budget. A third child was disallowed by the frozen protocol. This is an observed recovery limitation, not an environmental failure.
product_and_environment_assessment.context_capacity: The failed provider call reported 9531 input tokens against the configured 1050000-token context. No ContextTooSmall or network failure is recorded for this incident.
product_and_environment_assessment.interpreter: The sibling ran AggregateTests successfully with the supplied absolute interpreter; the parent also executed the prescribed tests and CLI. Missing Python/dependencies are not evidenced as the failure cause.
product_and_environment_assessment.model_vs_code_causality: One Luna-high baseline pass and one Luna-high candidate failure do not isolate stochastic model variation from changed tool descriptions/host-state guidance. The observed proximate cause is the frozen 4096-output-token ceiling, not input compaction.
product_and_environment_assessment.no_protocol_relaxation: Prompt, fixtures, interpreter command, parent/child budgets and acceptance gates are retained; no budget increase, extra child allowance or rerun of R10 has occurred.

separate_rotation_regression.conclusion: The new tool-work guidance was unnecessarily inserted into a text-only session. The extra bytes correctly triggered compaction at the fixture boundary; the original complete-prefix assertion consequently failed. No rotation identity corruption was demonstrated.
separate_rotation_regression.subsequent_minimal_change: Emit work_contract only when actual tools are present; retain the original 4000 window and all old assertions, and assert the first actual no-tool provider request has no work_contract.
separate_rotation_regression.subsequent_validation: 33/33 relevant tests PASS, 0 skips, 115 source/test fingerprints unchanged during the run.
separate_rotation_regression.independence_from_r10: The tiny-window test issue and R10 worker output truncation have distinct direct causes. Fixing the former does not turn R10 into a pass.

concurrency_boundary.interpretation: Both children did run with overlapping lifetimes, but the parser ended in error. The frozen qualification counts completed-child overlap only and remains failed; diagnostic terminal overlap is not substituted for that gate.

failed_receipt_classification.independent_root_causes: Do not count these four failed-status receipts as four separate implementation bugs.
